newsitem.title: CHINA: Sun Fook Kong in shr swap, property deal.
newsitem.headline: Sun Fook Kong in shr swap, property deal.

text.p: Sun Fook Kong Holdings Ltd has agreed to issue 31.28 million new shares in exchange for 20 percent of the enlarged share capital of Wah Tak Fung Holdings Ltd, Sun Fook Kong managing director Albert Chow said.

Sun Fook Kong, which will change its name to Hing Kong Holdings Ltd, also agreed to buy 90 percent of its parent China Travel International Investment Hong Kong Ltd's interest in a luxury residential property project in Tai Po for HK$509 million, Chow told reporters on Tuesday.
The consideration would be satisfied by the issue of 108.11 million new Sun Fook Kong shares at HK$4.71 each, he said.
China Travel, which has made a general offer for Sun Fook Kong shares after it bought 51.66 percent of the construction concern, has a one-third stake in the Tai Po project.

"According to the previous agreement, China Travel will from time to time inject property assets into Hing Kong and the company itself will aggressively develop its Hong Kong and China property and infrastructure businesses," Chow said.

In the share swap, Sun Fook Kung will issue 31.28 million new shares to Wah Tak Fung at HK$7.50 each in return for 138 million new Wah Tak Fung shares or 20 percent of the enlarged share capital of the company at HK$1.70 per share.
The 31.28 million new shares represented less than two percent of Sun Fook Hong's enlarged share capital, Chau said.
He said the agreements were still awaiting approvals from the stock exchange and the Securities and Futures Commission.
"It is good timing to enter into China property market since the market, which has been quiet during last past few years, is likely to bottom out soon," Chow said.
Trading in shares of Wah Tak Fung and Sun Fook Kong was suspended on Tuesday afternoon at the companies' request pending an announcement.
Shares of property and investment group Wah Tak Fung jumped HK$0.125, or 5.68 percent, to close Tuesday morning at HK$2.325.
Sun Fook Kong shares lost HK$0.35 to HK$7.50 before trading was suspended.
